I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou — the soil, the weather patterns, the wells. My family depends on what I grow, so I don't take risks with new methods I don't trust.

My 20 mu splits naturally: about 12 mu I rotate wheat and maize on the same plots — winter wheat goes in October, maize follows right after the June harvest. That's the backbone. Cash comes from the other 8 mu: 4 in chili and 4 in cotton, planted in spring.

**Wheat:** I use an improved variety — one of the Jimai lines that's been reliable here for years. I irrigate three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I apply urea in two doses, base fertilizer before planting and topdress at jointing. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in winter, then something for aphids and powdery mildew before harvest. I use rotary tillage after the maize comes off in October.

**Maize:** I buy hybrid seed from the county supply cooperative every year — Xianyu or similar, whatever has performed well locally. After the wheat harvest I seed directly without ploughing, saves time and moisture. I only irrigate if it's dry at tasseling or grain fill — usually twice is enough with the well. I spray herbicide early and watch for corn borer.

**Chili:** Planted by transplant in late April. These need water and attention. I irrigate six times through the season. Aphids and disease hit hard some years, so I spray five times to be safe. Heavy feeder, I push the fertilizer.

**Cotton:** Spring planting, plough the bed first. Cotton has the most pest pressure of anything I grow — bollworm, aphids, spider mites. Six pesticide passes is normal. I've been growing cotton long enough to know skimping on sprays costs more than the spray does.
